glossary_subset.notes: Os oito generais de Yamato. Ozen e um deles.
(cap.20) REI de Uzurusha; unificou 100+ tribos nomades. MASCULINO. Fonte: wiki.
Nome dado ao protagonista por Kuon em 11_02 (0x12668). reveal_timing: cena 11_02. Antes disso ele é sem nome.
Rótulo de falante (memória); identidade não revelada — genérico.
(cap.20) Nacao/regiao que caiu para Uzurusha. manter_original.
Soberano de Yamato ('o grande Mikado'); presenteou o moinho a vila. No cap.12 = o imperador/titulo. SPOILER: identidade pessoal e reveal posterior — NAO antecipar. reveal_timing: alem do cap.12.
(cap.19) Um dos Oito Generais-Pilar, 'o Sabio'; frio e calculista. MASCULINO. Lore profunda (vinculo familiar/arco) = beyond_frontier.
(cap.20) Pais/imperio nomade ao NORTE de Yamato; horda invasora. manter_original. Fonte: wiki.
(cap.20) Gentilico/soldado de Uzurusha. 'Uzurushan army' -> 'exercito uzurushano'; manter 'Uzurushan' como etnia.
(cap.20) Gentilico de Yamato (ja coberto). 'Yamatan army' -> 'exercito de Yamato'; 'yamato' invariavel. Forma derivada, nao entidade nova.
Nacao/estado onde se passa o cap.12; composta de muitas provincias; capital = sede do Mikado. Manter.

lines: Características: acolhe sem pressionar ("Apenas relaxe..."); curiosa mas paciente; calor humano.
Red flags: soar fria, clínica ou impaciente; formalidade excessiva.
Haku (protagonista, narração 1ª pessoa) — `voice_criticality: high`. Predomina nas 2 cenas:
Características: sentenças curtas e definitivas; duplo sentido ("um mundo totalmente novo te espera"); ambiguidade ameaçadora.
Red flags: soar caloroso/paternal; resolver a ambiguidade (a fala deve permanecer dúbia).
Registro: erudito cômico, pomposo e arcaico; bajulador do Ukon; alívio cômico.
Características: fala arcaica/empolada (equivalente a "vós/peço-vos/meus olhos não me enganam") + gag de cicio (s→sh, ex.: "SHEEKETH"/"shir"); melodramático; gruda no Haku como "benfeitor".
Red flags: perder o arcaísmo ou o cicio (são a piada); soar moderno/neutro; explicar a comédia. Manter o contraste entre a pompa do vocabulário e a fragilidade do personagem.

Oshtor — `voice_criticality: high`. = Ukon até 13_08 (ver spoiler_ledger). Registro formal, nobre, comedido; General da Direita. Antes do reveal, traduzir como o mercenário "Ukon" (espirituoso, informal) — NÃO antecipar a pompa de general
Características: frases quebradas por reticências; perguntas curtas ("Quem... é você...?"); pouca pontuação forte.
Red flags: falas fluentes/articuladas demais; perder o tom de torpor; pontuação "limpa" que apaga a fragmentação.
Registro: guerreiro carismático, espirituoso, caloroso e informal; líder nato que trata Haku como um irmão mais novo.
Características: desembaraçado, brincalhão, generoso; fala direta e cativante; autoridade leve (lidera a Coorte) sem arrogância.
Red flags: soar rígido/formal/militar demais (a graça é justamente o contraste com a patente); frieza. SPOILER: não deixar a tradução insinuar a identidade verdadeira — no cap.12 ele é só "Ukon".

decisions.title: Opcode de RÓTULO DE FALANTE `53 00` + reconcile de speaker (data-driven)
decisions.summary: **Problema:** in-game, o rótulo de falante aparecia em **inglês** ("Girl") mesmo com a tradução ("Garota") aprovada e gravada. RE: o nome do falante usa um **2º opcode de ponteiro, `53 00`** (mesmo formato file-relativo do `50 00` de diálogo), que o conector ignorava. Resultado: "Girl"→"Garota"

decisions.title: Gate de charset pt-BR — método e veredito
decisions.summary: **Decisão tomada:** Marcar `target_charset_supported: likely` e exigir confirmação in-game antes de produção. **Alternativas consideradas:** - Confirmar por presença no texto-fonte — **insuficiente**: o fonte é inglês e quase não usa acentos (só `õ` e `À` aparecem em texto real).

decisions.title: Anomalia 0x33f9 — texto PT/EN corrompido na fonte
decisions.summary: **Decisão tomada:** Marcar a linha `0x33f9` como anomalia de fonte (não traduzir em cima do lixo; tratar como linha de sistema reescrita). **Razão:** A string original já vem misturada PT/EN e truncada ("...SISTEMAS AM . RESTARTING...") no próprio jogo. Não é erro de extração. O conector deve sinali

decisions.title: Charset — transliteração na gravação (gate FALHOU)
decisions.summary: **Decisão tomada:** Marcar `target_charset_supported: false` e **transliterar** (acento → ASCII) na gravação do binário. A tradução canônica (`approved_translations.csv`, `translation_plan.json`) **mantém os acentos** (correta para QA/revisão); apenas os bytes escritos no jogo são dobrados para ASCI

decisions.title: Escopo cognitivo — 75 → 1025 linhas (cenas 11_01 + 11_02); reveal de Haku in-corpus
decisions.summary: **Decisão tomada:** Re-rodar o pipeline completo em escala (cenas 11_01 + 11_02 = 1025 linhas). Novos termos canônicos: **Kuon** (nome revelado em 0x108db), **Haku** (nome dado ao protagonista em 0x12668 — reveal agora **dentro do corpus**), **Tatari** (criatura imortal), **aperyu** (vestimenta), **

decisions.title: CORREÇÃO CRÍTICA — ponteiros são FILE-RELATIVOS, não absolutos
decisions.summary: **Decisão tomada:** Ao investigar o "opcode de início de bloco", descobri que **`50 00`+uint32 é um offset RELATIVO ao início do arquivo (Pack)**, não absoluto. Endereço da string = `file_start_do_site + uint32`. Prova: dos ~47k sites, **42.101** só apontam para string como file-relativos vs **63**

lines.source: From what information we have, it may be safe\n
to assume that Maruruha has fallen...\n
Most regrettable.
That concludes our report on the situation as it\n
stands. Now, we begin the emergency council.
My liege, we could not gather all Eight Pillar\n
Generals on such short notice. I beg your\n
forgiveness...
You have my pardon. Thank you all for your\n
haste and understanding.
The Mikado looks down from his throne,\n
surveying all those before him.
So... Maruruha has fallen to Uzurusha.
If all proceeds as predicted, Uzurusha will\n
doubtlessly progress onward with their invasion.
They are extremely well-supplied. I am led to\n
believe that they have a vast army at their\n
command.
It seems we have been ensnared by the very roads\n
we built...
Yamato's roads are its veins, its lifeblood, and\n
its prosperity... My liege, you must not despair.
Indeed...
The Mikado answers with curious detachment,\n
looking off into the distance as though\n
distracted.
Uzurusha... Formerly a loose territory of around\n
a hundred tribes; not truly a nation.
This was because the majority of the tribes were\n
nomads, traveling in search of arable land.
However, the arid climate of Uzurusha did not\n
provide for much fertile soil.
The tribes often warred among themselves,\n
battling to control what little land could be\n
cultivated.
Burdened with famine and poverty, they longed for\n
the lush soils of Yamato--soil they needed in\n
order to survive.
At times, raiding parties would pillage the people\n
of Yamato, who grew to see them as barbarians.
Despite the raids... There were very few instances\n
in which the Uzurushans clashed with Yamato's\n
military.
Their primary goal was to obtain resources.\n
They would only raid storehouses, or take the\n
Yamatans' harvested crops.
The Uzurushans knew they would stand little\n
chance if they drew the full brunt of Yamato's\n
ire.
However, with the appearance of one man,\n
the situation changed completely.
Gundhurua... a man who united over one hundred\n
tribes to create a mighty nation in one\n
generation.
After unifying the Uzurushans, he set his gaze on\n
invading surrounding nations... And now, Yamato.
Though not as prosperous, with an army of veteran\n
warriors, their forces vastly outnumber Yamato's.
Because most of Uzurusha's bordering nations\n
were not expecting a full-on invasion...
...they fell one by one, unable to muster a\n
retaliation in time.
Although Yamato drove them back, the Uzurushans\n
savored their brief victory. Their assaults\n
continued, their ferocity renewed.
And the lands they took became wastelands, with\n
no hope of restoration...
Gundhurua... The so-called 'great man' who\n
unified the barbarians and raised Uzurusha to\n
nationhood.
But... he is a fool.
To bare fangs against Yamato... Such audacity.\n
Does he truly think he stands a chance at\n
victory?
If he aims to be our jester, then let us indulge\n
him and laugh.
Such disregard is unlike you, Lord Raiko.\n
Underestimation of their ability may be your\n
downfall.
Humbling indeed, that I should be admonished by\n
you. Perhaps I must reconsider my expectations...
Your words of caution are, I assure you,\n
duly noted.
Ha... Hahaha.
The Uzurushan army is showing signs of\n
organization, as is their chain of command.
Rather than relying on sheer force of numbers,\n
it would seem they are employing sophisticated\n
tactics and strategy.
Strategy, you say...?
The Mikado faintly smiles, as though he has\n
just heard something amusing.
...What a cold smile.
Through every defense of the capital, I have\n
taken control of countless battles...
And for my merits, I am now one of the Eight\n
Pillar Generals, known as Guardian of the\n
Imperial Capital.
Yet not once before have I seen my liege smile so\n
when facing war...
The plight of his suffering people must fill him\n
with rage.
The fault is mine, for letting the situation\n
escalate to push my liege to such emotion.\n
Such shame...
Soldier
Reporting!
What is the meaning of this disruption!?\n
You are in the presence of our liege!
Messenger
This is an urgent matter! The Uzurushans have\n
crossed the border and begun their invasion!
What? Where was the defense force?\n
I thought we stationed enough troops to handle\n
them!
Sir, the defenders could not counter an assault\n
from all major roads! They remain under siege!
They're coming from all major roads...?
I have heard they take hostages, and force their\n
families to fight for them... as expendable\n
soldiers.
I had thought that they had learned to behave\n
themselves...
But it appears... they have yet to learn their\n
place.
The Mikado mutters, pity in his voice.
It seems this owlo of barbarians does not know\n
Yamato's true power. Perhaps pride can drive a\n
man mad.
Ah, my liege. Please, give me your orders!
I promise you, your graciousness, the barbarians\n
will crumple before my genius and might.
Be silent.
Nyeh...?
Wha--Wh--Wh--Wh... How dare you talk to me like\n
that! Who do you think I--
I will not repeat myself.\n
Close your foul mouth.
Nyeh... p-peh...
Great Mikado, we await your orders.\n
You need but give the word, and we will\n
eliminate all opposition.
That will not be necessary.
Tell the owlo of the barbarians this.\n
If he offers me his own head, I shall show mercy\n
to his people.
And if he should refuse your benevolent proposal,\n
my liege?
I am not a ruler without mercy. But I am not so\n
indulgent as to let such folly go unpunished.
Those that refuse to learn must be made to learn.
I give you permission to unleash your power.
Destroy them. Let all witness the price of their\n
ignorance.
All in the room bow their head at the Mikado's\n
cold proclamation.
Outright extermination... I confess, the prospect\n
brings me unease...
That is the will of our liege. We must destroy\n
all who bring harm to our nation.
Well, at least this should keep me entertained\n
for a while...
With permission to release their powers, the\n
other Eight Pillar Generals seem keen for battle.
I will need Haku and the others' help to keep us\n
from suffering innocent casualties...
